name: Backtracking
description: Backtracking is a systematic way to iterate through all possible configurations of a search space. It builds candidates incrementally and abandons ('prunes') a partial candidate as soon as it cannot possibly lead to a valid solution.
how_to_identify: Problems that enumerate all combinations, permutations, or subsets, or that build solutions incrementally where early decisions limit later ones.
use_cases: Generating all subsets, permutations, and combinations
Letter combinations of a phone number
template: A recursive function that, at each step, chooses a candidate, recurses, then 'undoes' the choice (backtrack). Optionally sort and skip duplicates and add pruning conditions to cut the search tree.
time_complexity: Often exponential, e.g. O(n ⋅ n!) for permutations
space_complexity: O(N) recursion depth plus O(N) for the current path
common_mistakes: Forgetting to undo a choice after recursion, polluting later branches.
Not skipping duplicate values after sorting, generating duplicate answers.
related_problems: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
